claims.claim: **Advice around the clock: phone 13 11 26 (Victorian Poisons Information Centre).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most adolescent recreational-drug presentations involve alcohol, often with other agents.** The page covers the acute issues only.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Amphetamines: a small dose may cause significant toxicity.** Sympathomimetic effects — agitation, sweating, tachycardia, hypertension. ⚠️ **Complications:** seizures, severe hyperthermia, hyponatraemia, cerebral oedema, rhabdomyolysis, intracranial haemorrhage.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Investigate:** 12-lead ECG, BSL, CK, troponin, electrolytes and renal function; **if vascular dissection is a worry, consider intracranial imaging.** **Manage:** a safe, low-stimulus setting · **cardiac monitoring, continuously** · **benzodiazepines for agitation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cannabis effects are dose related:** mild sedation, euphoria and disinhibition, progressing to CNS depression, anxiety and psychotic symptoms, postural hypotension and tachycardia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Benign symptoms → supportive care until symptom-free · anxiety → diazepam · cardiovascular effects → IV fluids.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **GHB causes CNS and respiratory depression progressing to coma**, with bradycardia and myoclonic jerks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **GHB: manage in a resuscitation area; expect it to improve within 4–6 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hallucinogens (Datura / angel's trumpet, magic mushrooms, LSD)** listed with an **anticholinergic toxidrome**: delirium, agitation, hallucinations, tachycardia, mydriasis, dry flushed skin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Supportive care; treat delirium with titrated diazepam.** ⚠️ **Antipsychotics such as haloperidol may worsen anticholinergic symptoms.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Inhalants act like alcohol** — euphoria and disinhibition, then CNS depression. ⚠️ **Complications:** sustained 'high', encephalopathy and seizures, methaemoglobinaemia, **cardiac arrhythmia and sudden death.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat behavioural disturbance or delirium with diazepam.** ⚠️ **In cardiac arrest, limit exogenous adrenaline.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Opioids: CNS and respiratory depression with miosis.** Dextropropoxyphene — seizures and arrhythmias; **tramadol — seizures and serotonin syndrome.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor for CNS and respiratory depression; airway protection and ventilation ensure a good outcome.** **Naloxone infusion** — note its short half-life. **Seizures: benzodiazepines and phenobarbitone.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recreational drug use and overdose' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recreational_drug_use_and_overdose/, retrieved 2026-09-23
